## p189 — Apparent vehicle request / await orders

**Edition context:** p189 — Vehicle request and orders to wait.

**Related source pages:** [p185 C](185.md#source-p185-c).

<a id="edition-cases-p189-p189--vehicle-request-and-orders-to-wait"></a>



**Status:** conditional partial source-linked reading of **p189 section A**. **Key:** Nov13–15b. **Contribution:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026, located the clearer p185 C near-parallel and audited all source-preserving alignments.

<a id="edition-cases-p189-most-likely-associated-message"></a>

### Most likely associated message

**Readable German — body excerpt from the associated message; no full p189 recovery asserted:**

> Gestellung [Auto] unmoeglich. Befehl abwarten. […]

**Meaning:** Providing a motor vehicle is impossible; await orders. The final signature or reference is garbled.

**Notes:** This is the most plausible interpretation of the clearer **p185 C near-parallel**, with `AUTU` normalized to `AUTO`. Its application to p189 is conditional on the source relationship. p189 itself does not fix this whole sentence: its exact shared plaintext constraints are retained below. The separate transport conversation strengthens the subject-matter context without filling the challenge's missing coordinates.

The p185 record directly decrypts, without edits, to:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
GESTELLUNGAUTUUNMOEGLICHXBEFEHLABWARTENXIXVRENTE
```

</details>

This approximately says provision of `[AUTU]` is impossible and orders should be awaited. `AUTO` is a plausible interpretation, not a certified substitution. The ending remains garbled.

<a id="edition-cases-p189-what-p189-itself-supports"></a>

### What p189 itself supports

The original has 90 slots: 78 valid ADFGVX coordinates, six literal `U` glyphs, one `R`, and five dashes. The online normalization U→V is unsupported. Treating all twelve invalid/erased positions as unknown preserves the actual evidence.

Aligning all 90 source positions monotonically to p185's 96 slots, without deleting or changing any received symbol, gives ten optimal alignments. Each inserts six erased slots and retains fifteen valid-symbol disagreements. Their invariant singleton plaintext is:

**Conditional interpretation — invariant singleton template across the ten stated alignments:**

```text
G??T????N???TOUNUO?GLI?H0B?FEH?ABA??WC?XIX??TN??
```

The shared clear `1835` header and ciphertext similarity support a relationship. Reversed callsign direction and inconsistent reception times prevent treating complete message identity as established. The full p185 reading must not be relabeled as an exact p189 decipherment.

[Certificate](../../data/certificates/p189.json) · [p185 C](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p185_C.png) · [p189 A](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_A.png). The verifier recomputes every optimal alignment and all plaintext domains while preserving every received valid coordinate.


<a id="edition-cases-p189-transport-context"></a>

### Transport context

[Seven adjacent intercepts and two near-parallel pairs](#edition-cases-context-transport) now have source transcriptions and direct known-key checks. The p194/p196 transport order can be combined to retain 86 of 87 positions, including `HANAU`, with every chosen source variant recorded. The p185 D missing-group model yields a conditional 91/99-position reading, but its gap location is not cipher-forced. Neither finding determines further letters in the original p189 challenge target.

Two complete short native bodies report an expected return and discuss obtaining a vehicle. The first is unchanged; the second has four explicitly priced coordinate substitutions. The incomplete spelling RUECKUNFT, the literal 0100 field and the elliptical sense of VERSUCHEN remain visible.

## p189 C — Instruction to use the December key; IRRTUM

**Edition context:** p189 C — December-key instruction.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p189-c-p189-c--december-key-instruction"></a>


[Source image](../../sources/excerpts/childs_p189_C.png)

**Status:** A supplementary contextual message, outside the 22-target challenge.
The unchanged published `Nov13-15b` key fixes **61 of 62 raw plaintext positions**.
**Source transcription and present review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.
The period key retains [George Lasry's published attribution](../../data/keys.json).

<a id="edition-cases-context-p189-c-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> [Unloesbare Funksprueche] nach Dezemberschluessel entziffern. Irrtum.

**Meaning:** “Decipher unreadable radio messages using the December key.”
The separate closing word `IRRTUM` means “error” or “mistake.” Its precise
function in this transmission is not established. Word spacing, punctuation
and capitalization are editorial.

The two bracketed words need **two known-coordinate substitutions**, with no
erasure fills or changes to the key. The rest of the proposed text is directly
decoded. In particular, **DEZEMBER and IRRTUM are source-supported** despite the
printed **15 November 1918** date. The edition does not replace December with
November, correct the date, or infer a cancellation procedure.

<a id="edition-cases-context-p189-c-unchanged-source-reading"></a>

### Unchanged source reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
UNLOESBA?EHUNKSPRUECHENACHDEZEMBERSCHLUESSELENTZIFFERNXXIRRTUM
```

</details>

The unknown at plaintext index 8 uses square cell `VG`, whose remaining domain
is `234789QY`. `R` already occupies `FG`. The proposed `UNLOESBARE` therefore
requires a received-coordinate change; assigning `R` to the unknown cell would
violate the square's injectivity. The raw `HUNKSPRUECHE` likewise needs an
explicit change to become `FUNKSPRUECHE`.

| Source index, zero based | Printed | Proposed | Plaintext effect |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 23 | V | F | `VG` becomes `FG`, giving `R` at plaintext index 8. |
| 62 | A | D | `AA` becomes `DA`, giving `F` instead of `H` at index 10. |

The other **122 source coordinates are unchanged**. The candidate has the same
62 positions as the direct reading and re-encrypts exactly to the stated
two-substitution reconstruction. No missing square cell is completed.

transmission or supply new fixed letters to p132's damaged wording.

**Edition context:** Benzol-pump inquiry with an explicit missing-coordinate model.

The p189 D reading asks whether a benzol pump is available and requests a prompt answer. Its 102-coordinate analysis is conditional: the printed body contains 101 occupied positions, including one non-coordinate glyph, and the first row ends with a four-coordinate group. **Readable German — labels from the edited output, with editorial word spacing and punctuation:**

> Ist eine Benzolpumpe dort. Beschleunigte Antwort. Seifert.

**Meaning:** The sender asks whether a benzol pump is available there and requests an expedited answer. The closing is the explicitly reconstructed surname Seifert, with no first name or biographical identification added.

All indices are zero-based. The five boundaries around XVGF have these costs for the displayed complete word proposal:

Both choices produce the same completed ciphertext under the fixed key, but their source-to-model maps and missing-slot values differ. The primary display uses boundary 38; the alternative is not suppressed. This is a conditional minimum within the 102-coordinate model and chosen wording, not an exhaustive proof over other message lengths or plaintexts.

#### Two vehicles and two trailers — p189 E

**Readable German — conditional shared VG=2, with one invalid-coordinate fill:**

> Ja, Hebepumpe aus Blech. Kommen 2 Autos. Hier 2 Anhaenger.

The [award-class interpretation](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/README.md#the-award-class)
supplies **VG=2** to both count fields, at plaintext positions **26 and 37**.
The word `ANH?ENGER` has the partial pair `V?`, with the invalid printed `B`
at source position **81**. Filling it as **V** gives `ANHAENGER`. This takes
the native 94-slot message from **44 to 47/47** fixed positions: two digits
from the shared square and one ordinary-word fill, with **no observed-coordinate
substitution**. The source's `B` remains visible in the literal transcription.
Indices are zero-based. [Exact completion and source mapping](../../experiments/nov13_joint_completion/transport_certificate.json).

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-conditional-result"></a>

### Conditional result

Inserting five erasures before source index **55**, a printed group boundary, gives this exact partial plaintext:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source index 55:**

```text
STATMETXMARSCHIERTLCST?UT?SMORGEN1500UEBERDHFNXAB?A6SCHBE?EITSEIN?VS6GROV?AN?IERE?XBITTEF6EXSEIFERT
```

</details>

Under this geometry, **91 of 99 characters are fixed**. The eight unresolved positions consist of six positions touched by uncertain coordinates and two positions using unassigned square cells. The fixed portions include `MARSCHIERT`, `MORGEN1500UEBERDHFN`, and `SEIFERT`; malformed portions are retained literally. `DHFN` and `STATMET` are not expanded into place or station names.

This is a conditional result. The strongest composite language score selects position 55, but a conventional plaintext quadgram score selects position 57:

| Gap before source index | Composite ranking score | Plaintext quadgram mean |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 55 | 24.910328 | -6.041730 |
| 56 | 22.691041 | -6.070230 |
| 57 | 22.641029 | -5.987314 |

These are heuristic scores, not confidence probabilities. All 194 positions are arithmetically compatible with the received symbols. Positions 159 and 160 produce the same masked ciphertext because the inserted gap can exchange places with the existing unknown `Y` slot. There are 193 distinct masked ciphertexts. No plaintext character is fixed across all 194 geometries. The three leading composite-score candidates share 89 fixed characters, but that selected subset is not a confidence set.

<a id="edition-cases-context-transport-truck-movement-and-readiness"></a>

#### Truck movement and readiness

The [word-completion certificate](../../experiments/p185_readiness_completion/README.md)
restores the vehicle noun and readiness instruction within the existing gap-55
frame:

**Readable German — conditional excerpt; the ellipses omit the damaged opening and closing instruction:**

> […] marschiert Lastautos morgen 1500 ueber DHFN. Abmarschbereit sein. […] Seifert.

The wording concerns trucks moving the following day via `DHFN` and instructs
the recipient to be ready to depart. `STATMET`, the transmitted `1500` and the
closing command remain unexpanded in the exact text. The unusual word order
is preserved.

`LCST?UT?S → LASTAUTOS` costs two observed-coordinate substitutions and a fill
of the printed `Y`. `AB?A6SCHBE?EITSEIN → ABMARSCHBEREITSEIN` costs one
substitution and two fills inside the five-coordinate gap. The edition fixes
**95/99 positions**, up from 91; three inserted coordinates remain unknown.
The same conversation has native `LASTAUTO` in p198 C, `ABMARSCH` in p193 C
and `BEREIT` in p196 B. These support the vocabulary without establishing an
identical sentence in another reception.

### Independent transport context

Six additional source-checked intercepts decrypt directly with the same historical key. They retain every literal garble and unresolved square cell:

- **p193 E, November 14:** `KLEINERFEDERWAGENZU?ANHAENGENHIERXKOMMTAUTOX`
- **p194 A, November 14, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITCGDHFN1?00XWAGENBERE?THALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT`
- **p196 B, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEI?ERT`
- **p197 E, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00A?GEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSOHNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSE?FERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p198 C, November 15, header `CM v CZ`:** `LASTAUTO1?00ABGEFAHRENXICHBLEIBEMIT?MANNBISSONNTAGXALLESGUTEAUFWIEDERSEHENXSEHFERTXGRUSSBOCHO`
- **p189 E, November 15, header `CZ v CM`:** `JAHEBEPUMPEAUSBLECHXKOMMEN?AUTOSXHIER?ANH?ENGER`. This is a different intercept from the p189 challenge target.

The p194/p196 pair repeats `DHFN` and names `HANAU` as the march destination. It has 171 of 174 raw coordinates in common; disagreements are at indices 82 (`K/X`), 167 (`X/V`), and 173 (`D/G`). The p197/p198 pair agrees at 183 of 186 coordinates, differing at indices 59 (`V/A`), 63 (`A/V`), and 67 (`G/A`). Neither lorry-message copy supplies an exact `SEIFERT` signature; `SEHFERT` is not silently corrected.

For the transport-order pair, a separately labelled source-supported composite takes `X` at index 82 and `V` at index 167 from p196 while retaining p194's `D` at index 173. It reads:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional source-supported composite of the p194 and p196 witnesses:**

```text
ABTRANSPORTINVERABREDETERWEISEFREITAGDHFN1?00XWAGENBEREITHALTENXMARSCHZIELHANAUXSEIFERT
```

</details>

This composite fixes 86 of 87 characters. It makes an editorial choice
between disagreeing source witnesses, with every chosen value attested in
at least one. The certificate retains all four combinations of the two
disagreements between valid coordinates. The planned-time cell `FV`
remains unassigned.

Under the separate shared VG=2 interpretation, the reported-hour cell
`AF` cannot also be 2. If the departure occurred on the report's date
before its `13.45` origin time, `1?00` therefore becomes **13:00**. That
chronological assumption is kept separate from the source-supported
composite. The [linked-field comparison](197.md#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198-linked-number-fields)
also shows why this reading cannot be combined with the earlier extra
assumption that the reported departure was no earlier than the planned one.

The [certificate](../../data/certificates/p185_D_transport.json) contains every gap geometry, its full plaintext domains, exact source-to-plaintext mapping, all six direct context readings, both near-parallel comparisons, and the conditional composite. The [standalone verifier](../../adfgvx/transport.py) recomputes all 194 constraint sets and exact coordinate roundtrips without a language model. It checks the consistency of the stored ranking order but does not recompute the heuristic scores. The [portable ranking script](../../experiments/known_key/README.md) reproduces both complete rankings from a pinned upstream model; every stored score matched exactly in the recorded environment.

```sh
python3 -m adfgvx.transport
```

This analysis does not fully solve p189 and does not add a solved item to the 22-message total.

Four [additional p197/p198 witnesses](197.md#edition-cases-context-transport-197-198) now connect the
conversation with equipment for Darmstadt, a lorry, a trailer and a petrol
pump. Their duplicate-group and missing-coordinate hypotheses have separate
source and arithmetic certificates.
